title: Nine vanishing transients on 1950s plates, follow-up with Gran Telescopio Canarias
summary: Beatriz Villarroel tells of Nine vanishing transients on 1950s plates, follow-up with Gran Telescopio Canarias, about 1950 (plates); 2021 (study) at Palomar Sky Survey plates; Gran Telescopio Canarias, Canary Islands, and says they saw it or took part. As told, not a fact.
place_text: Palomar Sky Survey plates; Gran Telescopio Canarias, Canary Islands

tellings.quote: Uh we had this guy at Grand Telescope Canaria, one of my friends who actually pointed the world's largest optical telescope, a 10.4 m telescope to the positions of all these nine objects or eight of them or something like that and there was nothing left.

plain: Beatriz Villarroel, an astronomer, says that on old 1950s photographs of the night sky from the Palomar Sky Survey, a big photographic map of the sky made in California, she found nine points of light that were there and then vanished. She says a friend later pointed the Gran Telescopio Canarias, the world's largest optical telescope, 10.4 meters across, in the Canary Islands, at those spots and found nothing left. She tells it because, if real, these brief flashes may point to unknown objects in the sky in the 1950s.
